hook.text: Apply red dye, wipe it off, spray white developer — hidden cracks bleed red lines before your eyes.

buildup.text: Liquid penetrant testing uses capillary action to pull dye into surface-breaking cracks.

discovery.text: After cleaning the surface, a developer draws the trapped dye back out — revealing the crack pattern.

twist.text: It works on any non-porous material — metals, ceramics, plastics — no magnetism required.

climax.text: Gas turbine blades, ceramic insulators, and welded piping are all checked with dye penetrant.

punchline.text: A drop of dye and capillary action expose what the eye alone can't see.

quiz.question: How does dye penetrant testing reveal cracks?
options: Dye changes color when heated near a crack
Capillary action pulls dye into cracks, which bleeds out through developer
Dye reacts chemically with the crack surface
